object_title_english: Fish-shaped wrapped mummy containing a young crocodile
classification_basis: 1979 description + radiograph (Plate XXb): fish-shaped bundle (not crocodile-shaped) containing complete young crocodile; resin fillings
acquisition: Obtained in Egypt around 1900 by J. Zounek of Mrzky (district Kolín); given to Museum of Český Brod in 1930 (1979). Official site: trip to Egypt 1910

notes: Official museum page (2026) lists 'dvě malé egyptské mumie (krokodýl a poštolka)' from Zounek collection.

object_title_english: Wrapped cylindrical object with crocodile head (composite)
classification_basis: 1979 radiology: only skull of young crocodile present, body substituted by two boards and fillings
acquisition: Brought by Joseph Seilern, former owner of the castle, from his trips around the world 1929-31
description: Oblong wrapped cylindrical object from which the head of a crocodile and the distal end of the content jut out; head wrapped in rough ochre bandages with black spots. Radiology: skull of young crocodile; rest substituted with two long boards (27.5 and 29.7 cm); 'a fake - in the sense of filling up a large parts of the missing body'.
bibliography: Strouhal & Vyhnánek 1979, Egyptian Mummies in Czechoslovak Collections (Sborník NM XXXV B), p. 134, Cat. No. 120
notes: Tourism site zlinsko-luhacovicko.cz mentions 'mumii mláděte krokodýla' shown in Great Castle Library (probably this object).
